rounds.response:
Leading hypotheses: (a) transient stray-light/glint or bright-object in star-tracker 2 FOV causing degraded solution and loss-of-lock, (b) transient SEU/processing glitch inside the tracker yielding a temporary bad solution, and (c, less likely) an external micro-impulse or estimator/software anomaly (ruled low by absence of thruster/pressure signatures and config changes).  
The ~90 s wheel-current ramp before the lock loss implies ACS was already trimming for a slowly increasing attitude uncertainty or disturbance that may have made the tracker more vulnerable, so I assign moderate confidence to (a)/(b) and low confidence to (c).  
Operational risk is currently low for immediate harm (no limits crossed) but medium until we rule out an attitude-dependent stray-light condition or intermittent hardware fault that could recur under similar geometry.  
Immediate recommended checks: retrieve and inspect raw star-tracker frames ±120 s around the event, pull high-rate raw gyro and magnetometer traces and wheel torque commands for correlated spikes, and correlate spacecraft attitude vs Sun/Moon/Earth geometry at the time; also fix the quick-look pipeline that produced the false RCS indication.  
Assumptions: clocks and independent recorder are trusted (confirmed); major uncertainty is lack of raw tracker imagery and high-rate sensor dumps—please authorize those buffer retrievals for a definitive root-cause determination.
